pairs.evidence: src/app/guide/[category]/[topic]/TopicView.tsx:144 The anchored-heading clearance is a local `scroll-mt-24` (96px) literal, kept outside the guide-chrome budget module. Below lg the fixed mobile TOC bar covers 78–122px, so a heading reached by an anchor jump lands underneath that bar.

techniques.evidence: src/components/guide/guide-markdown/parseGuide.ts:335 Each parse builds one stateful assigner (dedup map plus section-N fallback counter) and writes ids into the tree. The TOC (headingsOf) and the renderer both read from that tree. headingId.test.ts asserts DOM ids equal TOC ids over duplicates and emoji-only headings, and checks that those paths fired.

src/app/guide/[category]/[topic]/TopicView.tsx:144 guide-chrome.ts is a good budget module (measured constants, band diagram, lane, z-order). It does not own three things. (1) Heading scroll margin: scroll-mt-24 is also a literal in HeadingAnchor.tsx and does not clear the 122px mobile band. (2) Band top: -96px is a literal in useActiveHeading.ts. (3) Pinned-panel max height: the sticky TOC at TopicView.tsx:177 has no height bound.

src/app/guide/[category]/[topic]/TopicView.tsx:43 The guard is keyed on topic identity and held at module scope, so it survives Next remounting the segment. The h1 has tabIndex={-1} and a focus-visible outline. e2e/guide.spec.ts:147-151 checks both directions: focus does not move on cold load and lands on the h1 after navigation.

src/components/guide/useActiveHeading.ts:8 Most of the band is right: IntersectionObserver with a -65% bottom inset, topmost intersecting wins, and no intersection keeps the previous answer. But before anything is observed it defaults to the first entry, which the technique names as a failure. ReadingProgress uses whole-document useScroll(), so footer and related topics count toward progress. Two trackers run, one per TOC. The active entry has no aria-current.

src/app/guide/[category]/[topic]/TopicView.tsx:83 page.tsx:120-122 parses once on the server and passes initialHeadings down. The client re-extracts only when the body value differs. Minor gap: readingMinutes is computed client-side in TopicView rather than next to the server extraction.

pairs.evidence: src/app/blog/[slug]/BlogArticle.tsx:63 Reading time shown on the article is a number the author types by hand (src/data/blog.ts `readingTime: number`, e.g. `readingTime: 5,`). It is not derived from the body being rendered, so it drifts silently whenever the post is edited.

techniques.evidence: src/app/blog/[slug]/blog-article/BlogArticleContent.tsx:23 Posts render through the guide's parseBlocks to parseGuide, so the shared per-document assigner mints the ids that the heading copy-anchor links point at. There is only one consumer and no second id computation.

src/app/blog/[slug]/BlogArticle.tsx:38 The page has a fixed Navbar plus ReadingProgress (positioned with CHROME_TOP_PROGRESS from the budget). Navbar clearance, though, is a local h-24 spacer instead of the budget's CHROME_PAD_NAVBAR, and heading clearance is HeadingAnchor's literal scroll-mt-24. That makes independent estimates of one geometry.

src/app/blog/[slug]/BlogArticle.tsx:36 There is no scroll spy (no contents panel), but the reading-progress part applies. ReadingProgress uses whole-document useScroll(), and this page puts the byline, cross-links and <Footer /> after the body. The bar measures the document rather than the article body, which the technique names as a failure.

src/app/blog/[slug]/BlogArticle.tsx:63 The technique bans reading time 'as a value an author types in and forgets to update'. Here it is a hand-maintained field in src/data/blog.ts, not computed from post.content.
